Experiments on autoregressive video generation show improvements in long-horizon visual quality and temporal consistency, without changing the inference procedure.

items.title_en: Healthy Counterfactual Generation via Diffusion Inpainting for Mammography Classification
items.abstract_en: False negatives remain a critical limitation of computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems for breast cancer screening due to delayed detection and treatment. To address this issue, we propose a counterfactual data augmentation strategy that generates healthy mammograms by "erasing" lesions from anomalous images, thereby enriching the training distribution. We train a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model on BI-RADS 1 (healthy) mammograms and use a RePaint-based sampling strategy to inpaint realistic normal tissue within annotated lesion bounding boxes. The resulting healthy counterfactuals replace annotated lesion regions with realistic healthy tissue while preserving patient-specific anatomical structure, as supported by similarity metrics between real and generated images. Image realism was further assessed by radiologists and found to be consistent with the original dataset quality. We evaluate counterfactual augmentation across four representative classifier architectures: a convolutional neural network (ConvNeXt), a vision transformer (ViT), a vision-language model pre-trained on mammogram-report pairs (Mammo-CLIP) and a multi-scale attention-based multiple-instance learning framework (FPN-MIL). Experiments conducted on the VinDr-Mammo dataset show improvements in sensitivity across all architectures, particularly at 80\% fixed specificity, contributing towards more reliable CAD systems for breast cancer. Code is available at: https://github.com/ines03garcia/diffusion-based-counterfactual-generation.

items.title_en: LVS: Local View Synthesis from Relative Camera Pose by Reusing Previous Views
items.abstract_en: Interactive scene exploration requires frequent view updates, although small camera motions preserve much of the visible content. Conventional 3D Gaussian Splatting nevertheless renders each target view, leaving this image overlap unexploited. Reusing rendered images offers an alternative. Geometric warping alone cannot recover newly exposed content and remains sensitive to depth errors. We propose a per-scene framework that replaces repeated scene rendering for nearby views with relative-pose-guided RGB-D image reuse. Geometric warping uses depth and relative pose to transport source content, while a lightweight multiscale network predicts RGB residuals to correct artifacts and infer missing appearance. Cached source features further reduce repeated computation. On GS-render, residual refinement improves PSNR by 0.72~dB over pure warping; evaluations on captured and rendered scenes demonstrate low query latency. This separation of scene rendering from local view updates supports responsive scene exploration, with potential applications in augmented and virtual reality.

items.title_en: SuperNav: An Agentic Navigation System for Any Task in Any Scene
items.abstract_en: General-purpose service robots need navigation systems that can handle diverse human requests in unfamiliar environments, combining task generality with scene generality. Some existing methods fine-tune multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to predict navigation actions, making their behavior dependent on the coverage of navigation training data and potentially limiting generalization to new requests and environments. Our key insight is to let the MLLM focus on interpreting requests, understanding scenes, and making decisions while preserving its general-purpose capabilities and delegating motion execution to navigation tools. To realize this idea, we introduce SuperNav, which equips a pretrained MLLM with a specialized agent harness without navigation-specific fine-tuning of the MLLM. Our harness supports these decisions with Navigation Skills, agent-oriented Tools for physical interaction, and task-progress and context management. A unified visual-point interface connects decision-making to motion by allowing the model to specify destinations directly in images and revise its decisions from execution feedback. Together, these components support sustained navigation across different task requirements and environments. SuperNav outperforms four evaluated baselines on instance-level, multi-object, and demand-driven tasks. Category-level evaluation on HM3D and deployment on a real quadruped robot further demonstrate its applicability across environments. Project Page: https://zju3dv.github.io/SuperNav/

items.title_en: ContourVLA: A Closed-Loop Perception-Action Contour Policy for Generalized Referring Expression Segmentation
items.abstract_en: Generalized referring expression segmentation (GRES) requires dynamically balancing high-level semantics for identifying a variable number of language-specified referents with fine-grained visual evidence for precise boundary delineation. This requirement challenges existing cascaded vision-language architectures, which typically rely on static feature interfaces and single-pass mask prediction, limiting adaptive perception and geometric correction. We introduce ContourVLA, a vision-language-action policy that recasts GRES as a closed-loop visuomotor process, in which editable contours serve as explicit policy states that condition multimodal perception and are updated by geometric action chunks. Evolution-Aware Semantic Scheduling (EASS) couples contour-guided bidirectional boundary sampling with state-conditioned routing of multilevel multimodal features, adapting perception to each contour state. Following supervised initialization, Dustbin-Augmented Entropic Credit Transport GRPO (DECT-GRPO) jointly optimizes discrete grounding and continuous contour actions with instance-level credits. Its rollout rewards and credits are derived from soft prediction-target correspondences that account for false positives and missed targets. ContourVLA improves gIoU over the strongest evaluated baselines by 8.7, 2.8, and 2.7 points on gRefCOCO val, testA, and testB, respectively, and achieves the highest mIoU across all eight RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg splits.

items.title_en: VINCIE-NExT: Unlocking Video Editing from Images via In-Context Modeling
items.abstract_en: Building a capable video editor remains significantly harder than a video generator: editing requires (source, instruction, edited) triplets that are prohibitively expensive to annotate and difficult to synthesize at scale, whereas image editing has already reached maturity with millions of such pairs readily available. In this work, we introduce VINCIE-NExT, a unified framework that transfers editing capability from images to videos through in-context visual demonstrations, alleviating the need for large-scale paired video editing data. VINCIE-NExT decomposes video editing into a structured chain of composable sub-tasks (Video -> Image -> Image -> Video), routing editing intent through the image domain and enabling scalable joint training from heterogeneous image and video corpora under a unified diffusion objective. An image editing pair, synthesized by the model or supplied by the user, is prepended as an in-context visual demonstration that serves as a spatial appearance blueprint for every output frame. To ground appearance edits across the interleaved context, we introduce a novel position encoding that links image demonstrations and video frames in a shared spatial coordinate system, enabling pixel-faithful propagation of appearance changes to every output frame. Chain-of-Editing further provides principled test-time scaling: by executing the sub-task chain as progressive diffusion stages, editing quality can be improved by investing additional compute without retraining. Comprehensive experiments on OpenVE-Bench demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance across diverse editing categories, with ablations confirming the effectiveness of each component.

items.title_en: Few-Step Generation via Data-Space Iteration
items.abstract_en: Flow matching has emerged as a scalable paradigm for training high-quality generative models, but sampling from the learned probability flow requires many network evaluations. Distillation can reduce this cost to one or a few evaluations; however, one-step generation often sacrifices quality, making few-step generation the practical operating regime. Existing few-step methods perform their iterative computation along the probability flow and therefore require a fixed, manually chosen timestep discretization. This discretization is often chosen heuristically and is expensive to tune; it may also be restrictive when refinement difficulty differs across samples or spatial locations. We introduce data-space iteration, a few-step generation framework that removes flow discretization altogether. Starting from noise, a shared generator directly refines its prediction in data space, with every iteration trained to produce the best sample permitted by its capacity. Our formulation integrates with distribution matching distillation (DMD) with minimal changes, enabling a controlled comparison between iteration methods under matched training settings. On class-conditional ImageNet 256x256, data-space iteration outperforms standard discretization baselines and matches or improves upon variants selected through schedule search, without requiring schedule-specific training. These results show that data-space iteration provides a simple and effective alternative to discretized flow-space iteration for fast generation.

items.title_en: DVLA-RL++: Dual-Level Vision-Language Alignment with Reinforcement Learning Gating for Few-Shot Learning
items.abstract_en: Few-shot learning aims to recognize novel categories from limited labeled examples. Recent studies incorporate textual semantics to compensate for limited visual observations and improve class representations. However, high image-text agreement may reflect both intrinsic object properties and incidental context, making support prototypes susceptible to contextual contamination. To address this problem, we propose DVLA-RL++, which extends DVLA-RL with complementary semantic purification (CSP) and counterfactual reinforcement-learning gating (CRG). Specifically, CSP generates intrinsic and nuisance descriptions from labeled supports and compares their agreement with each support token. An ambiguity-dependent rejection margin guides sparse evidence allocation, while an intrinsic semantic anchor fills the unassigned mass to provide a fallback when visual evidence is unreliable. CRG learns layer-wise semantic fusion strengths using a reward that balances recognition performance and nuisance exposure. An independently executed reference trajectory on the same episode provides a paired learning signal. Theoretical analysis relates retained evidence and anchor quality to prototype stability and establishes conditions for unbiased on-policy gradient estimation. Experiments on standard, fine-grained, and cross-domain benchmarks show state-of-the-art accuracy, with an average gain of 1.4% over DVLA-RL. The project page is available at https://peacelwh.github.io/TPAMI27-DVLA-RLpp/.

items.title_en: Perception Test 2026: Challenge Summary and Extension to City-scale Audio-Visual Reasoning
items.abstract_en: Continuing the Perception Test challenge series, we organised the fourth edition as a workshop at the European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV) 2026 in Malmö, Sweden. This edition focused on spatial intelligence and featured four different tracks: unified multiple-choice videoQA and grounded videoQA from the original Perception Test benchmark, alongside two new tracks based on city-scale walking-tour videos (KilometerAudio and KilometerVision). In this report, we describe the new benchmarks used for the city-scale tracks and summarise the winning solutions across all tracks, including a generalist model that competed across all tracks with satisfactory performance. The winning solutions in the newly added city-scale tracks demonstrated that complex spatial and multimodal reasoning can be solved by expensive agentic pipelines, but remains difficult for multimodal models used standalone.

items.title_en: A Minimal Optical-Flow Representation for Vision-Based Tactile Rotation Classification in Robotic Manipulation Across Gravity Domains
items.title_zh: 一种用于跨重力域机器人操作中基于视觉的触觉旋转分类的极简光流表示
items.abstract_en: Vision-based tactile sensors provide rich contact information, but processing high-resolution images can be costly for resource-constrained platforms such as space robots. This work investigates whether a compact representation of tactile motion can classify object rotation across different gravity conditions. Dense optical flow from a simulated GelSight Mini is aggregated over a 7x9 grid into 126 features and used to classify the direction of load-induced rotation under Earth, Mars, Moon, and orbital gravity. Gravity causes a small but significant shift in these features, accounting for 1.6% of their variance (R2 = 0.016). Despite its small magnitude, this shift affects models trained only on Earth data: XGBoost accuracy decreases from 94.4% on Earth to 75.9% in orbit. In contrast, a single model trained across all four gravity domains achieves 96.3% overall accuracy and 95.1%-97.0% across individual domains, without using gravity as an input. The representation can also be reduced to 40 features while retaining 95.7% accuracy, with XGBoost requiring only 0.14 ms per inference. These findings show that Earth-gravity performance alone is insufficient to establish the transferability of tactile perception for space robotic manipulation, highlighting the need to account for gravity-induced domain shifts during training and validation.

items.title_en: LIVIN: Benchmarking Spatial and Embodied Intelligence in Digital Twins of Lived-In Homes
items.abstract_en: Realistic household simulation must capture not only diverse environments but also the lived-in object arrangements and spatial constraints that shape robot motion and interaction. Existing resources often trade off scale, real-world correspondence, and interaction readiness, leaving a gap in faithful, interactive replicas of how real homes are actually arranged. To this end, we introduce LIVIN, a benchmark for spatial and embodied intelligence built on digital twins of 30 diverse lived-in homes. These replicas preserve observed room layouts, furniture configurations, and everyday belongings. To construct them, we design a human-in-the-loop workflow comprising instance recognition, architectural reconstruction, and object generation and placement, with intermediate results reviewed and corrected by humans against the source observations at each stage. We evaluate four tasks in LIVIN: 3D detection, 3D reconstruction, navigation, and loco-manipulation. Our evaluations show that current methods remain challenged by the dense object arrangements, occlusions, limited free space, and constrained interaction regions found in realistic lived-in homes. We hope LIVIN will help advance embodied AI in real-world homes, from spatial understanding to robotic interaction, and ultimately bring embodied intelligence into everyday home environments.

items.title_en: Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning
items.abstract_en: Processing long visual token sequences from high-resolution images makes multi-step reasoning computationally expensive for multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). Existing one-shot pruning and aggregation methods compress visual tokens into a fixed context before decoding. However, visual evidence needs can shift as reasoning unfolds, making it difficult for a fixed compressed context to retain all the details needed across stages. To address this challenge, we propose ViMoD, a lightweight framework that maintains a compact visual context while preserving access to original fine-grained evidence as reasoning needs evolve. Deformable Aggregation of Region-wise Tokens (DART) learns content-adaptive groups and aggregation capacities, constructing compact Coarse representations linked to recoverable original Fine tokens. Temporal Routing for Adaptive Contextual Evidence (TRACE) integrates decoding history to anticipate upcoming evidence needs and select, retain, or replace active Fine-token groups. Selected Fine tokens augment the persistent Coarse context in the frozen backbone, enabling stage-specific evidence access without continuously attending to all visual tokens. On Qwen3-VL-4B, ViMoD outperforms all evaluated baselines on all eight reasoning benchmarks at a 20% target visual token budget, improving the mean normalized score by 39.0% over the strongest evaluated one-shot baseline. These gains are achieved with only 0.0546% additional trainable parameters relative to the frozen backbone.

items.title_en: FearCaut-Qwen: Affective Steering in a Vision-Language Model Shifts the Decision Criterion for Hazard Assessment
items.title_zh: FearCaut-Qwen：视觉语言模型中的情感引导改变危险评估的决策标准
items.abstract_en: Vision-language models (VLMs) show great potential for damage assessment after a disaster, but a recurring deficiency is that they are reluctant to declare a hazard; that is, recall is low even when overall accuracy appears adequate. This study examines that deficiency by using signal detection theory to decompose the decision behavior into perceptual capability and decision-criterion placement. We then propose a novel method for correcting the over-conservative decision policy, inspired by the finding that fear makes humans risk-averse, and ask whether an affective representation associated with fear can be causally manipulated to similarly alter a VLM's decision tendency. Using mechanistic interpretability, we localize a causally implicated affective circuit in the model and use activation steering to manipulate it while observing the effect on downstream prediction. The method is tested on a two-stage SeisMLLM pipeline built on Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, which flags only 27.0% of genuinely unsafe buildings on the SeisMLLM-1K test split and never issues a false Red, an SDT criterion of c = +1.354, despite adequate evidence quality (d' = 1.521). An affective direction is localized on emotion-rich natural scenes, causally validated by sparse-neuron knockout and distributed steering on held-out emotion data, and then injected into the building task. Fear-direction injection raises Red recall to 75.7% (p<0.001), and subtracting the same direction suppresses Red predictions entirely, whereas norm-matched random and matched happiness directions show no significant effect. The mechanism is a shift in criterion (c=-1.515) while discrimination is not improved (d'=-0.493). These results show that VLM decisions can be adjusted at inference time without retraining and demonstrate how mechanistic interpretability can be used to diagnose and control VLM decision behaviors in engineering applications.

items.title_en: Learning Which Correspondences to Trust: Confidence-Weighted Event-Camera Localization in LiDAR Maps
items.title_zh: 学习信任哪些对应关系：LiDAR地图中置信度加权的事件相机定位
items.abstract_en: Localizing an event camera against a pre-built LiDAR map can be cast as dense optical-flow estimation between a rendered depth view and an event image, followed by a Perspective-n-Point (PnP) solver over the induced 3D-2D correspondences. Existing pipelines rely on geometric consensus during pose estimation, but do not explicitly model the reliability or pose informativeness, i.e., how strongly a correspondence constrains the camera pose, of individual correspondences. We show that the natural way to learn it -- using the per-correspondence error to constrain the learning of confidence -- suffers from a depth-dependent bias: small pixel errors reside predominantly at large depths and do not lead to high pose informativeness. Instead, in our method (CELL), we learn a per-correspondence confidence end-to-end through the pose, using a differentiable probabilistic PnP whose log-partition term encourages weight configurations that yield a better-constrained pose distribution. The learned confidence is used in three ways: (i) it reweights the flow supervision in a decoupled training scheme that keeps pose gradients out of the flow/edge backbone; (ii) it drives a probabilistic correspondence selection at test time; and (iii) together with the network's edge-probability it weights a final edge-matching refinement. We further design a partial-completion depth representation that adds signal without hallucinating across large gaps. On M3ED and DSEC our full system improves over the LEAR baseline on the majority of the evaluated sequences: it reduces the median translation error by up to 26.9% and the median rotation error by up to 15.8%.

items.title_en: A large, comprehensive labeled MRI dataset of the human lateral ventricle choroid plexus
items.title_zh: 一个大型、全面的侧脑室脉络丛人工标注MRI数据集
items.abstract_en: The choroid plexus (ChP) is a highly vascularized structure located in the brain ventricles that plays important roles in multiple central nervous system functions. ChP enlargement has been implicated in many neuropsychiatric conditions such as multiple sclerosis, depression, schizophrenia, and Alzheimer's disease. However, limitation in the accuracy of the current segmentation tools highlight the need for more reliable methods to quantify ChP volume in healthy and clinical human populations. The shape and size of the ChP vary drastically from person to person, and currently there are no large ChP datasets which allow comprehensive training of segmentation models. Here we introduce DataPlex, a collection of 700 structural MRI brain images where the lateral ventricle ChP has been manually labeled and checked by expert human raters. DataPlex is balanced and representative across a wide range of scanning parameters, demographics, and clinical profiles, and subject-level information will be available for each labeled image. DataPlex will be open source to support the creation of reliable segmentation tools for the human lateral ventricle ChP.
items.abstract_zh: 脉络丛（ChP）是位于脑室内的高度血管化结构，参与多种中枢神经系统功能。ChP增大与多发性硬化、抑郁症、精神分裂症和阿尔茨海默病等神经精神疾病相关，但现有分割工具精度不足，亟需更可靠的方法量化健康与临床人群的ChP体积。ChP形态个体差异极大，目前尚无足以全面训练分割模型的大型数据集。为此，我们构建了 DataPlex：包含700例结构MRI脑图像，其侧脑室ChP已由专家人工标注与核查，在扫描参数、人口学与临床特征上均衡且具代表性，并附被试层面信息。该数据集将开源，以支持可靠分割工具的开发。
items.highlight_zh: 首个大规模、专家人工标注的侧脑室脉络丛MRI数据集
items.digest_zh:
1）研究了什么问题：脉络丛（choroid plexus, ChP）位于脑室内、血管丰富，与多种脑功能相关；它的体积增大多见于多发性硬化、抑郁、精神分裂症、阿尔茨海默病等疾病。要研究这种关联，必须先能准确地把ChP从MRI图像里分割出来并测量体积。但ChP形状大小因人而异，现有自动分割工具精度不够，而训练更好的AI模型又缺少大规模人工标注数据，形成“先有鸡还是先有蛋”的困境。
2）用了什么方法：作者公开了 DataPlex 数据集，包含700例结构性脑MRI，每例的侧脑室ChP都由专家人工标注并复核。数据集在扫描参数（不同机器与序列）、人口学特征和临床背景上都做了均衡与代表性设计，每张标注图像还附带被试层面的信息。
3）有什么结果：得到一个规模大、标注可靠、覆盖面广的ChP资源库，并以开源方式发布。
4）为何重要：为开发可靠的ChP自动分割工具提供了训练与评测基础，有望推动“ChP体积”作为神经精神疾病生物标志物的研究，让不同研究之间的测量结果可比较。

items.title_en: Differential utilization of PACAP and glutamate in parabrachial neurons shapes pain and stress
items.title_zh: 臂旁核神经元中PACAP与谷氨酸的差异化利用塑造疼痛与应激
items.abstract_en: The external parabrachial nucleus (elPBN) contributes to diverse behaviors, including pain and stress. Neurons in this region use glutamatergic and neuropeptidergic signaling, with pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide (PACAP) expressed in a subset of glutamatergic neurons. Deletion of PACAP in elPBN neurons attenuates behavioral responses to stress, but the contribution of PACAP to pain sensitization and of glutamatergic neurotransmission to pain- and stress-related responses remain poorly understood. Here, we show that constitutive loss of PACAP markedly attenuated nerve injury-induced hypersensitivity across heat, pressure, cold and tactile modalities without altering baseline nociception, while also reducing inflammation-induced spontaneous pain-related behavior. Notably, selective deletion of PACAP within elPBN neurons phenocopied the suppression of injury-induced hypersensitivity, but left inflammation- induced pain-related behavior unaffected. Ex vivo optogenetic-assisted circuit mapping showed that activation of PACAP-expressing elPBN terminals elicited glutamatergic transmission onto central amygdala (CeA) PKC{delta}-expressing neurons. Selective deletion of VGluT2 in elPBN neurons reduced nerve injury-induced hypersensitivity but, unlike PACAP deletion, also reduced inflammation-induced pain-related behavior, while leaving stress-induced hypophagia intact. Together, these findings reveal differential requirements for PACAP and glutamatergic neurotransmission within the elPBN across pain- and stress-related behaviors.
items.abstract_zh: 外侧臂旁核（elPBN）参与疼痛与应激等多种行为，其神经元兼具谷氨酸能与神经肽能信号，PACAP（垂体腺苷酸环化酶激活多肽）表达于部分谷氨酸能神经元。此前已知敲除elPBN的PACAP可减弱应激反应，但PACAP对疼痛敏化的作用及谷氨酸能传递的贡献尚不清楚。本研究发现，缺失PACAP显著减弱神经损伤诱导的热、压力、冷和触觉超敏而不改变基线痛觉，并减少炎症性自发痛行为；在elPBN内选择性删除PACAP可重现该效应，但不影响炎症性痛行为。光遗传环路图谱显示，PACAP阳性elPBN终末可驱动向中央杏仁核PKCδ神经元的谷氨酸能传递。删除elPBN的VGluT2同样减轻损伤性超敏，但还减少炎症性痛行为，且不影响应激性厌食。这些结果揭示elPBN内PACAP与谷氨酸能传递在疼痛和应激行为中的差异化需求。
items.highlight_zh: elPBN中PACAP主导神经损伤痛，谷氨酸能传递兼顾炎症痛与应激
items.digest_zh:
1）研究了什么问题：脑干外侧臂旁核（elPBN）是处理疼痛和应激的关键枢纽，其神经元主要用谷氨酸（兴奋性递质）和神经肽传递信号，其中一部分谷氨酸能神经元还表达神经肽 PACAP。此前知道 PACAP 与应激反应有关，但它在疼痛中的作用，以及谷氨酸能传递分别负责哪些行为，一直不清楚。
2）用了什么方法：作者用基因敲除小鼠，分别全身性或仅在 elPBN 神经元中删除 PACAP；另外删除 elPBN 的 VGluT2（谷氨酸能囊泡转运体，等于切断谷氨酸释放）。行为学上测量神经损伤后的热、压力、冷、触觉超敏，炎症性自发痛行为，以及应激性厌食。再用离体光遗传辅助环路图谱追踪 elPBN 到中央杏仁核（CeA）的连接。
3）有什么结果：删除 PACAP 能缓解神经损伤引起的各类超敏，却不影响基线痛觉；只在 elPBN 内删除 PACAP 就足以产生该效果，而且它只作用于损伤性痛，不影响炎症性痛。光遗传图谱显示，PACAP 阳性 elPBN 神经元的轴突终末能向 CeA 中表达 PKCδ 的神经元释放谷氨酸。删除谷氨酸能传递（VGluT2）既缓解损伤性痛，也缓解炎症性痛，但应激性厌食完好无损。
4）为何重要：说明疼痛、炎症痛和应激虽都经由同一核团，却由 PACAP 神经肽信号与谷氨酸信号分工负责。这为理解“痛”与“应激”在神经环路层面如何分道扬镳、并据此开发更有针对性的干预手段提供了依据。

items.title_en: The anterior insular cortex mediates higher-order threat learning and memory
items.title_zh: 前岛叶皮层介导高阶威胁学习与记忆
items.abstract_en: Learning about potential threats is indispensable for survival, and its deficits underlie numerous neuropsychiatric disorders. Human brain imaging suggests the anterior insular cortex (AIC) as a key neural correlate of threat learning, yet its mechanistic role remains unclear. Leveraging multimodal systems neuroscience approaches, we demonstrate that AIC excitatory neurons, specifically layer 5 pyramidal neurons projecting to the basolateral amygdala, are essential for higher-order threat learning/memory. They are specifically required when a predictor is temporally separated from an aversive event or when the predictive information is embedded within a diffuse context. In contrast, the AIC is dispensable for elementary, temporally contiguous threat learning. Surprisingly, while the AIC promotes memory formation, it also constrains the level of fear expression during retrieval in a context-dependent manner. This bidirectional control is mediated by the recruitment of distinct AIC neuronal ensembles. Together, we identify a novel circuit mechanism for bidirectional regulation of higher-order threat learning/memory.
items.abstract_zh: 学习潜在威胁对生存至关重要，其缺陷是多种神经精神疾病的基础。人脑成像提示前岛叶皮层（AIC）是威胁学习的关键神经关联区，但其机制作用仍不清楚。我们结合多模态系统神经科学方法，证明AIC兴奋性神经元——特别是投射到基底外侧杏仁核的第5层锥体神经元——对高阶威胁学习/记忆不可或缺。当预测线索与厌恶事件在时间上分离，或预测信息嵌入弥散背景中时，这些神经元是必需的；相反，AIC对基本的、时间连续的威胁学习并非必需。出人意料的是，AIC虽促进记忆形成，却在提取阶段以依赖背景的方式限制恐惧表达水平。这种双向调控由不同AIC神经元集群的招募介导。总之，我们揭示了一个双向调控高阶威胁学习/记忆的新环路机制。
items.highlight_zh: 前岛叶第5层至杏仁核环路双向调控高阶威胁学习与恐惧表达
items.digest_zh:
1）研究了什么问题：能否学会预判危险直接决定生存，这种能力的缺陷与焦虑症、创伤后应激障碍等精神疾病密切相关。人脑影像早就把前岛叶皮层（AIC）与威胁学习联系起来，但它究竟是因果上“必要的环节”，还是只是同步活动的“旁观者”，一直不清楚。
2）用了什么方法：作者在小鼠上结合多模态系统神经科学手段（针对特定投射通路神经元的活动操控与行为学范式），把“简单”威胁学习（预测线索与电击在时间上紧挨着）和“高阶”威胁学习（线索与厌恶事件间隔较久，或预测信息藏在弥散的背景中）区分开来，并重点追踪 AIC 第5层投射到基底外侧杏仁核的锥体神经元。
3）有什么结果：AIC 的兴奋性神经元，特别是投射到基底外侧杏仁核的第5层锥体神经元，只在“高阶”情境下必需；对时间连续的基本学习则可有可无。更意外的是，AIC 在记忆形成阶段“帮忙”，但在记忆提取阶段反而“踩刹车”，以依赖情境的方式限制恐惧表达的强度。这种“一手促进、一手限制”的双向作用由不同的 AIC 神经元集群分别执行。
4）为何重要：研究把 AIC 从“相关脑区”升级为高阶威胁记忆的关键因果节点，并揭示同一脑区内部的不同神经元集群可实现方向相反的调控，为理解焦虑障碍中恐惧记忆过度泛化的机制提供了环路层面的线索。

items.title_en: Ordinal position in auditory sequences is encoded in population dynamics in macaque frontal cortex
items.title_zh: 听觉序列中的序数位置编码于猕猴额叶皮层群体动态中
items.abstract_en: The ability to extract structure from sensory sequences requires tracking not only stimulus identity but also ordinal position within a sequence. How and where ordinal information is represented in the primate brain remains unclear. Here, we recorded activity in populations of single neurons simultaneously from auditory cortex and ventrolateral prefrontal cortex in macaques passively listening to structured auditory sequences. Population-level analyses revealed that frontal cortex activity evolved progressively across the sequence, occupying distinct regions of neural state space for successive ordinal positions. In contrast, auditory cortex population activity reset with each element, producing stereotyped, stimulus-locked trajectories. Consistent with this dissociation, frontal cortex populations robustly decoded ordinal position independently of stimulus identity, whereas auditory cortex showed weak positional decoding despite strong identity representations. Frontal neurons further exhibited longer intrinsic timescales and reduced synchronization to element presentation, supporting integration of information across multiple elements. Together, these findings identify frontal activity as a key substrate for ordinal position encoding during auditory sequence processing, while auditory cortex primarily supports element-specific sensory representations.

items.title_en: A human CHRNA6 3' UTR variant alters the molecular environment and microRNA engagement of the adolescent VTA without changing Chrna6 transcript abundance
items.title_zh: 人类CHRNA6 3' UTR变异改变青少年VTA的分子环境和microRNA结合，而不改变Chrna6转录本丰度
items.abstract_en: A single nucleotide polymorphism (rs2304297) in the 3' untranslated region (UTR) of CHRNA6, encoding the alpha6 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunit, is associated with adolescent smoking behavior. Humanized rats carrying the 'C' or 'G' allele show sex- and genotype-dependent responses to adolescent nicotine, yet the variant does not alter the protein sequence and the mechanism has remained unknown. We examined the molecular consequences of rs2304297 in vivo in the adolescent ventral tegmental area (VTA). Chrna6 transcript abundance did not differ by genotype, nor did transcript stability or polyadenylation site selection. The variant was instead associated with a transcriptional signature spanning myelin maintenance (Enpp6), lipid metabolism (Retsat), and genomic repair (Polq), and with elevated basal lipid peroxidation in alpha6GG animals. Computational folding predicted greater conformational flexibility of the 'G' allele, and spatial colocalization of Chrna6 with miRNA-365-5p was reduced in alpha6GG animals of both sexes. Coordinated expression of the two transcripts, however, followed a sex-by-genotype pattern, absent in alpha6CC females and alpha6GG males. These same groups showed elevated tyrosine hydroxylase expression and dopaminergic neuron number, and expansion of the Chrna6 co-expression network following nicotine. We propose that rs2304297 acts through two distinct layers: genotype determines spatial engagement of miRNA-365-5p with the transcript, while sex determines whether that engagement produces functional regulation. These findings identify a post-transcriptional mechanism for a non-coding nicotine addiction risk variant and demonstrate that its molecular effect can be uniform while its consequences are not.

items.title_en: rpSTS Stimulation Disrupts Shared Neural Responses to Social Content during Naturalistic Viewing
items.title_zh: rpSTS刺激干扰自然观看过程中对社会内容的共享神经反应
items.abstract_en: Shared understanding of common experiences can foster feelings of social closeness and friendship, and help us understand those experiences. Recent work has suggested that patterns of neural activity shared across individuals, especially throughout the default mode network, may underlie shared representations. Here we used repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) and functional magnetic resonance imaging during movie watching to show that shared neural patterns to common experiences rely on the encoding of social information from the environment by the right posterior superior temporal sulcus (rpSTS). An encoding model of movie features showed that rTMS selectively degraded social feature encoding in rpSTS, leaving low-level visual encoding in early visual cortex intact. Using natural language processing (NLP)-based analysis, we found that rpSTS stimulation was associated with reduced memory and intersubject pattern similarity across DMN and limbic networks during scenes central to the movie narrative. Projecting scene embeddings onto NLP-based concept axes revealed reductions in memory and neural pattern similarity for scenes conveying helplessness and empathy following rTMS. These findings provide causal evidence that the rpSTS is a key region that encodes shared social information into common neural representations, and suggest that disrupting its input leads DMN representations to become idiosyncratic.

items.title_en: Disrupting the Right Inferior Frontal Gyrus Increases Social Brain Activity During Emotion Recognition
items.title_zh: 干扰右侧额下回增加情绪识别期间的社会脑活动
items.abstract_en: Neuroimaging studies have identified a specialised social brain network that supports emotion recognition and social cognition. This network performs a range of functions that include facial expression recognition and inferring the mental states of others. Studies of neuropsychological patients report that damage to the right inferior frontal gyrus (IFG), the top-down control area in this network, impairs facial expression recognition. To investigate how transient disruption of the right IFG affects the wider social brain we combined transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) with functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). Participants (n=20) were scanned across two sessions while performing a delayed match-to-sample emotion recognition task in which happy or fearful expressions were preceded by a congruent or incongruent word cue. Prior to each scan, thetaburst TMS was delivered over the right IFG or over the vertex control site (session order was balanced across participants). A group whole-brain analysis revealed that TMS to the IFG increased neural activity in multiple regions of the social brain network. These included the bilateral temporal pole, precuneus and medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC). This pattern of results shows that the disruption of top-down control mechanisms localised in the IFG alters the neural processing in remote nodes of the social brain network. Our findings are discussed within the wider context of how we recognise and understand the emotions of other people.

items.title_en: Developmental prefrontal myelination shapes inhibitory interneuron function and adult social behavior
items.title_zh: 发育期前额叶髓鞘化塑造抑制性中间神经元功能和成年社会行为
items.abstract_en: Early-life adversity and abnormal myelination are implicated in psychiatric disorders, but how developmental myelination influences adult social cognition remains unclear. Here, we tested whether disrupting developmental myelination in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) impairs adult social behavior. Using complementary genetic strategies in male mice, we suppressed Myelin Regulatory Factor (Myrf)-dependent myelination locally in the juvenile mPFC or broadly in oligodendrocyte-lineage cells. Both approaches selectively impaired adult social novelty preference while sparing sociability, locomotion, and affective behaviors. Focal prefrontal dysmyelination also reduced social dominance. Spatial transcriptomics revealed coupling between myelin-related genes and parvalbumin (PV) interneuron markers in the healthy mPFC, which was disrupted by developmental hypomyelination. Consistent with this transcriptional alteration, PV interneurons showed reduced high-frequency firing despite preserved intrinsic excitability. In the human prefrontal cortex, MBP-PV expression was correlated in controls but not in individuals with schizophrenia. These findings indicate that developmental prefrontal myelination contributes to PV interneuron maturation and suggest that disrupted oligodendrocyte-interneuron coordination may contribute to impaired social recognition.

items.title_en: EARLY-LIFE STRESS INDUCES SEXUALLY DIMORPHIC BRAIN AGING VIA MESOLIMBIC ALTERATIONS AND FRONTO-STRIATAL DYSFUNCTION
items.title_zh: 早期生活压力通过中脑边缘系统改变和额纹状体功能障碍诱导性别二态性脑衰老
items.abstract_en: Prenatal stress influences brain development; however, its long-term, region-specific effects on brain aging in males and females remain insufficiently characterized. This study examined the impact of unpredictable mild prenatal stress on behavior, cognition, and maternal care in C57BL/6J mice at middle (12 months) and old (18 months) ages. Stressed dams showed fragmented, unpredictable maternal behaviors, creating a stressful postnatal environment without impairing caregiving capacity. Both male and female offspring were born with lower birth weights and showed rapid postnatal growth, a trajectory associated with central insulin resistance and hippocampal signaling deficits. Sex-specific behavioral differences emerged with age. Middle-aged stressed males exhibited anhedonia, which progressed to hyperactivity, stereotypy, and persistent spatial memory deficits in old age. These outcomes corresponded with accelerated fronto-striatal decline, likely mediated by insulin resistance and increased rigidity of medial prefrontal cortex structures due to diminished local estrogenic activity. In contrast, middle-aged stressed females displayed hypoactivity and reduced anxiety, later developing anhedonia in old age while maintaining hippocampus-dependent memory. In females, this pattern supports a model in which a neuroestrogen - and growth factor-dependent feedback loop transiently preserves hippocampal plasticity but compromises dopaminergic function in reward circuits. This balance may deteriorate with reproductive senescence. Both sexes retained cognitive flexibility, indicating domain-specific rather than global cognitive impairment. These findings demonstrate that excessive prenatal glucocorticoid exposure and unpredictable postnatal care produce a combined hormonal and metabolic insult, resulting in sexually divergent trajectories of brain aging. The results underscore the necessity of incorporating sex as a biological variable in fetal programming research across the lifespan.

items.title_en: Hemispheric Complementarity is Associated with Distinct Functional and Structural Brain Profiles
items.title_zh: 半球互补性与不同的功能和结构脑特征相关
items.abstract_en: Hemispheric specialization is thought to follow a principle of complementarity, with homotopic functions such as language and attention lateralizing to opposite hemispheres, yet its consistency across individuals and relevance for cognition remain unclear. Using multimodal neuroimaging and twin-family data from 987 Human Connectome Project participants, we identified three sustained attentional lateralization phenotypes (right, left, bilateral) that were independent of handedness, differed by sex, and tracked broad shifts in brain organization, with bilateral individuals showing stronger intrahemispheric and homotopic connectivity. Examining attention and language revealed three multidomain profiles (crowded, mixed, split) reflecting whether functions colocalize within or are distributed across hemispheres. Mixed organization was linked to higher planum polare myelination, whereas crowded organization showed higher fiber density connectivity across dorsal attention-default network. Both phenotypes were heritable, yet neither predicted cognitive performance. These findings reveal a brain organization in which specialization emerges from flexible, heritable patterns linking function, structural connectivity, and myeloarchitecture.

items.title_en: Attention warps visual-semantic representations across the human cerebellum
items.title_zh: 注意扭曲人类小脑中的视觉-语义表征
items.abstract_en: Humans effortlessly shift their attention between objects and events in the environment. These attentional shifts modulate the representation of information in many regions of the cerebral cortex, including those that represent visual-semantic information. Based on recent evidence that the cerebellum also represents semantic information, we hypothesized that attention would also shift semantic representations in the cerebellum. To test this hypothesis, we used fMRI to measure brain activity while participants watched naturalistic movie clips and were instructed to attend to either people or vehicles. We used a voxelwise encoding model framework to recover visual-semantic representations in the cerebral cortex and cerebellum under the two conditions, and quantified the direction and magnitude of visual-semantic tuning shifts between conditions. Attention to different semantic categories had a large effect on visual-semantic tuning in the cerebellum. Representations in some regions shifted toward the attended category, and representations in other regions shifted away from the attended category. Within cerebellar regions that best represent visual-semantic information, the tuning shifts were most pronounced in Crus I and II and in lobule VI. Further, the magnitude of attentional tuning shifts was greater in the cerebellum than in the cerebral cortex, particularly for tuning shifts towards the attended category. These differences suggest that attentional modulation in the cerebellum is different than in the cerebral cortex and may not solely be driven by cerebral inputs.

items.title_en: Domain-specific and domain-general signatures of dyscalculia in computational models of behavior and parietal cortex
items.title_zh: 行为和顶叶皮层计算模型中计算障碍的领域特异性和领域一般性特征
items.abstract_en: Developmental dyscalculia is a learning disorder characterized by marked difficulties in numerical cognition, yet its cognitive and neural underpinnings remain debated. Competing accounts attribute dyscalculia either to domain-specific imprecise representations of number or to domain-general deficits in the maintenance and integration of numerical information. Here, we test both accounts in 33 adolescents and young adults with dyscalculia and 33 age- and gender-matched controls (15-23 years) who performed a sequential numerosity comparison task during fMRI. Joint computational modeling of choices and response times allowed us to dissociate perceptual and memory noise from decision variables governing the speed-accuracy tradeoff, while complementary neuroimaging analyses characterized neural number representations and their network embedding. Specifically, we quantified the precision of parietal numerosity tuning with numerical population receptive field (nPRF) modeling and derived individualized functional network maps of the same region using community detection algorithms applied to connectivity patterns. Dyscalculic participants showed greater perceptual and memory noise but also a more cautious response criterion, trading speed for accuracy to compensate for representational imprecision. Neurally, the numerosity model explained less variance in parietal cortex, suggesting less precise numerical representations, and individualized network maps assigned less of this cortex to the dorsal attention network and more to a visual network. Rather than supporting a dichotomy between the two accounts, our findings suggest that dyscalculia reflects both less precise numerical representations in parietal cortex and an altered allocation of this cortex to distributed functional systems.

items.title_en: Mapping the Trade-Offs That Shape Mammalian Brain Network Architecture
items.title_zh: 绘制塑造哺乳动物脑网络架构的权衡关系
items.abstract_en: A brain's wiring must satisfy conflicting pressures, from the outside world (be capable) and from the inside (stay within finite resources). These pressures often have opposing requirements. Prior work studies these trade-offs mostly between 2-3 pressures at a time, and thus cannot say how many pressures shape brain wiring or for which trade-off brains decide. To see all possible trade-offs at once and to uncover the set of most important pressures, we generate 25,000 synthetic brain networks and describe each by 29 network properties. We then place 635 human (ages 6-22) and 224 mammalian (12 taxonomic orders) brain networks in this property space. The space is triangular, and follows three pressures: computational capability, robustness to damage, and metabolic efficiency. No network is optimal at all three, and biological brains cluster in one small niche of this triangle. There, they accept higher metabolic cost to gain both robustness and capability. Development and evolution move brains in the same direction; additionally, human maturation first raises capability, and later optimizes for efficiency. This study underscores the triangular trade-off between metabolic efficiency, computational capacity and robustness, and the narrow region brains occupy in this trade-off triangle, visible only from a multi-property, cross-species perspective.

items.title_en: Intragenic epistasis in couch potato shapes life history traits and climatic adaptation in Drosophila melanogaster
items.title_zh: couch potato 基因内上位性塑造黑腹果蝇的生活史性状与气候适应
items.abstract_en: Populations adapting to heterogeneous environments often harbor many alleles that covary with environmental gradients, yet how so many adaptive variants can be maintained and show signatures of local adaptation remains unclear. Epistatic non-additive interactions among alleles may concentrate fitness effects at specific allelic combinations to shape complex traits and facilitate adaptation. We evaluate compositional epistasis among three intronic SNPs in the couch potato (cpo) gene, each independently clinal along the North American latitudinal gradient, using recombinant outbred populations fixed for distinct three-locus combinations. Flies carrying all three temperate alleles (cpoTTA) or all three tropical alleles (cpoCGT) show non-additive increases in traits associated with fitness in their respective environments: dormancy, starvation resistance, and lipid storage in temperate flies and fecundity in tropical flies. Intermediate genotype combinations generally show weaker and negative deviations from additive predictions. Temperate genotypes show reduced cpo expression and independently create predicted transcription factor binding sites, suggesting a regulatory basis for the observed phenotypic effects. Consistent with selection shaping haplotype frequencies against a backdrop of ongoing recombination, the temperate and tropical genotypes are enriched above random expectation across the latitudinal cline, with directionally consistent but non-significant seasonal patterns. Our findings demonstrate that non-additive interactions among non-coding variants within a single gene can produce large, pleiotropic fitness effects and shape genotype distributions in natural populations, providing a mechanism by which a small number of regulatory variants can underlie complex climatic adaptation.

items.title_en: Transcriptional perturbation effects remain structured beyond the leading global trend
items.title_zh: 转录扰动效应在主导全局趋势之外仍保持结构化
items.abstract_en: Prior work has described a global transcriptional response to gene perturbation, with many perturbations moving cells along a common direction. We find that perturbations contribute differently to this leading global trend and that substantial organization remains beyond it, including transferable perturbation-specific effects across datasets and a common hierarchy of responsive genes across perturbations. These patterns make simple strategies surprisingly competitive even in predicting effects beyond the leading global component.

items.title_en: A multi-tissue transcriptome strategy for genomic resource development in Pinus edulis
items.title_zh: 用于 Pinus edulis 基因组资源开发的多组织转录组策略
items.abstract_en: Premise:: Conifers comprise one-sixth of global forests and landscape genomic studies are urgently needed to understand their biology, yet relatively few conifer species have reference genomes. Targeted exon-capture is a practical alternative to whole-genome sequencing, but selecting loci without a reference genome remains a barrier. We developed a multi-tissue reference transcriptome for pi non pine (Pinus edulis) to ask how multi-tissue sampling improves probe design, and what is lost under a conventional single-tissue approach. Methods: We assembled a reference transcriptome from four diploid tissues (needle, phloem, root, vegetative bud) and one haploid tissue (megagametophyte), using the latter as a pseudo-guide. We designed a target-capture probe-set by prioritizing highly expressed P. edulis transcripts and transcripts matching a conifer exon database. Results: We recovered 76% of conserved plant genes with few duplicated transcripts. Filtering yielded 15,664 transcripts totaling 31.4 Mb, ~0.1% of the genome. Tissue-specific expression was substantial: 27.4% of transcripts occurred exclusively in non-needle tissues. Functional annotation confirmed complementary contributions, including seed-desiccation and germination genes from megagametophytes, and defense- and stress-associated genes from roots and phloem. Discussion: We built a transcriptome and efficient probe set using a roadmap suitable for other non-model plants with large genomes; keys to success were prioritizing complementary tissues and using expression-based filtering.

items.title_en: From Sparse Visits to Continuous Molecular Trajectories with Flow Matching
items.title_zh: 从稀疏访视到基于流匹配的连续分子轨迹
items.abstract_en: Longitudinal transcriptomic studies often capture only a few molecular snapshots of each patient over time. This makes it challenging to understand how patients are progressing, compare them when progression rates differ, and capture molecular changes between observed visits. We introduce CohortFM, a flow-matching framework that reconstructs continuous patient-specific molecular trajectories from sparse longitudinal observations and organizes them through an integrated mixture model into a compact set of cohort-level progression patterns. CohortFM separates molecular progression from calendar time, places patients on a shared progression scale, uses observed intermediate states to guide the learned trajectories, and maps the resulting patterns back to real patient samples for biological interpretation. We evaluated CohortFM across COVID-19, sepsis, influenza, and tuberculosis. Despite different sampling patterns, the method generalizes well and consistently produces meaningful trajectories. These trajectories capture biological differences between patients that cannot be explained by the observed samples alone. Compared with state-of-the-art trajectory baselines, CohortFM produces more biologically distinct trajectories and a more complete representation of the patient population. Its finer progression scale also reveals biological programs and temporal dynamics that are not captured by visit-level analysis. We further evaluated interpolation and true forward prediction to test whether CohortFM can accurately recover unobserved states. CohortFM remains competitive with strong interpolation baselines and is among the strongest learned predictors in the harder forecasting setting. Ablation experiments further show that flow matching is the core learning mechanism and that our design choices improve continuous trajectory learning. Our results support CohortFM as a practical framework for turning sparse molecular snapshots into continuous, biologically interpretable trajectories. By going beyond visit labels, CohortFM makes it possible to study disease progression and predict future molecular states even when patients are sampled only a few times.

items.title_en: Autonomous AI agents discover reverse transcriptases with tandem repeat arrays
items.title_zh: 自主AI智能体发现带有串联重复阵列的反转录酶
items.abstract_en: Metagenomic databases hold vast quantities of unexplored genetic material that can seed tools for biotechnology and medicine, but discovery is limited by our ability to examine sequence data at scale. Here, we show that large language models (LLMs) in an autonomous harness can alleviate this bottleneck and surface novel molecular systems. We deployed Claude Code instances to survey reverse transcriptase (RT) loci across 1.9 billion protein clusters. Among the top candidates were array-associated RTs (ART), a novel family of jumbo-phage RTs coupled with an array of ~200-nucleotide units and a dedicated partner gene. Session transcripts show that Claude identified the ART family by directly examining its DNA sequences and recognizing the atypical repeats, a behavior attributable to specific Mythos 5 internal signals that respond to repeated DNA. ART arrays are highly expressed and appear as discrete units during Staphylococcus phage infection, suggesting an RT system directed by a repertoire of distinct RNAs. These findings indicate that LLMs can autonomously detect anomalies and drive analyses to initiate biological discoveries.
items.abstract_zh: 宏基因组数据库蕴藏大量未开发的遗传材料，可孕育生物技术与医学工具，但发现受限于我们大规模审阅序列数据的能力。本文表明，在自主框架中运行的大语言模型（LLM）能缓解这一瓶颈并挖掘出新的分子系统。我们部署 Claude Code 实例，在19亿个蛋白簇中系统筛查反转录酶（RT）位点。在排名靠前的候选者中，我们发现了阵列相关RT（ART）——一个新型巨型噬菌体RT家族，其与约200个核苷酸单位的阵列及一个专一伴侣基因相连。会话记录显示，Claude通过直接检查DNA序列并识别出这种非典型重复而发现ART家族，该行为可归因于 Mythos 5 中对重复DNA响应的特定内部信号。ART阵列表达量很高，在葡萄球菌噬菌体感染期间以离散单元出现，提示这是一个由多种不同RNA指导的RT系统。这些发现表明，LLM能够自主识别异常并驱动分析以开启生物学发现。
items.highlight_zh: LLM智能体自动筛查19亿蛋白簇，发现新型噬菌体反转录酶家族ART
items.digest_zh:
1）研究了什么问题：宏基因组数据库里存着海量未知基因，相当于生物技术和新药的“金矿”，但想从中找到有用的东西，需要把几十亿条序列挨个看完，人工根本看不过来，这成了关键瓶颈。
2）用了什么方法：作者把大语言模型（LLM）放进一个自主工作框架中——具体是部署 Claude Code 实例，让它在19亿个蛋白簇里系统性筛查反转录酶（RT）相关位点。模型不只是做分类，而是自己查看序列、提出并提出并追踪假设。研究者还回看了模型的对话记录，弄清它是怎么“发现”新家族的，并分析了让模型对重复DNA敏感的特定内部信号（Mythos 5 中的信号）。
3）有什么结果：模型找到了一个全新家族——阵列相关反转录酶（ART），属于巨型噬菌体RT，特征是带有一段由约200个核苷酸单位组成的串联重复阵列，还配有一个专属伴侣基因。记录显示，Claude 是通过直接阅读DNA序列、注意到这种异常重复而发现 ART 的。ART 阵列表达量很高，在葡萄球菌噬菌体感染期间以离散单元出现，提示它可能是一套由多种不同RNA引导的RT系统。
4）为何重要：这是“AI自主做出科研发现”的一个具体实例——LLM 不只是提速工具，还能自己注意到人类容易忽略的序列异常，主动把研究带向新方向，为挖掘宏基因组资源提供了新范式。

items.title_en: Continuous amyloid staging complements global amyloid burden in early Alzheimer's disease
items.title_zh: 连续淀粉样蛋白分期补充早期阿尔茨海默病中的全局淀粉样蛋白负荷
items.abstract_en: Introduction: Early Alzheimer's disease (AD) staging remains challenging because clinical categories and global amyloid PET measures provide only coarse characterization of disease progression. We developed a continuous amyloid staging score from regional amyloid PET to complement global amyloid burden. Methods: Using longitudinal florbetapir PET from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), we trained an end-to-end deep learning model to directly estimate a continuous amyloid staging score. We evaluated longitudinal consistency, its relationship with global amyloid burden, regional contributors to early-stage variation, and whether the staging score stratified subsequent memory decline among participants matched for baseline global amyloid burden. Cognitive analyses were replicated in A4+LEARN. Results: The staging score better preserved longitudinal visit order than existing amyloid staging approaches. During early disease stages, it captured regional amyloid variation despite relatively stable global amyloid burden. Among participants with similar baseline global amyloid burden, higher staging scores were associated with faster subsequent memory decline in both ADNI and A4+LEARN. Discussion: A continuous amyloid staging score complements global amyloid burden for early AD staging and cognitive risk stratification. Keywords: Alzheimer's disease; amyloid PET; disease staging; cognitive decline

items.title_en: Genetic Variant Burden Rises with BMI: Insights from Rare and Low-Frequency Variants in Obesity
items.abstract_en: Adult obesity, including morbid obesity, has reached epidemic proportions worldwide. Yet, the current genetic models based on BMI-associated common variants identified through genome-wide association studies (GWAS) explain only a modest fraction of BMI variability. Contribution of rare and low-frequency variants to polygenic obesity remains incompletely defined. Leveraging whole-exome sequences of 1138 adults spanning normal-weight, overweight, obese and morbidly obese (MO) categories from Kuwait and Qatar, we catalogued cohort-specific rare and low-frequency deleterious variants differentiating MO individuals from normal-weight individuals. Cross-cohort comparisons identified 147 risk variants seen in [≥]2 MO individuals from one cohort and in [≥]1 MO individual from the other; among these, 27 variants occurred in [≥]2 MO individuals from each cohort. The risk genes were enriched in obesity-related pathways and tissues, with most harbouring GWAS variants associated primarily with obesity traits followed by metabolic and brain-related traits. Duodenal tissue expression data exhibited significant dysregulation of key risk genes in MO individuals. Variants from the 147-list and 27-list occurred in 87% and 49% of MO individuals, respectively; MO-variant burden correlated positively with BMI (r=0.30 and r=0.31, respectively) across the overweight-obese-MO categories. Combinations of a finite set of low-frequency coding variants substantially shape the continuum of polygenic obesity.

items.title_en: Do Calibrated-Probability Claims Hold Up in Clinical Diagnosis? A Pre-registered Evaluation of a Decision Model Against Frontier Language Models
items.abstract_en: Background: A new class of AI "decision models" returns a probability for every option in a single pass and is marketed as calibrated, which invites use in clinical triage. Whether those probabilities hold up on clinical diagnosis has not been independently tested. Objective: To test the diagnostic accuracy, calibration, and probabilistic coherence of a decision model (Jev 1.13, TypeSafe AI) against frontier language models, with and without reasoning. Methods: In a pre-registered study (OSF, registered 26 September 2026), we compared Jev with Claude Opus 5.5 (adaptive reasoning, always on) and Claude Opus 5 (reasoning disabled) on three case sets: the 45 Semigran symptom-checker vignettes, 1,000 stratified synthetic patients from DDXPlus with reference differentials, and 80 simulated ophthalmic complaints (40 diagnoses at two levels of detail). Each model returned a probability for every diagnosis on a fixed list. Outcomes were top-1 and top-3 accuracy, expected calibration error (ECE), Brier score, the rate of exactly zero probability on the true diagnosis, sensitivity to option order, behavior on uninformative inputs, and behavior when the true diagnosis was absent. Results: On DDXPlus, top-1 accuracy was 72.0% for Jev, 79.5% for Opus 5 without reasoning, and 87.4% for Opus 5.5 (both comparisons with Jev P<.001). Jev assigned exactly zero probability to the true diagnosis in 62 of 1,000 cases (6.2%); neither comparator did so in any case. Calibration error did not differ between Jev and the registered comparator (ECE difference 0.007, 95% CI -0.026 to 0.038). Offered an explicit "none of these" option, Jev declined to diagnose all 30 uninformative inputs; without that option, it assigned a mean 58% to a single diagnosis. Order sensitivity was small in all models. Given the option list with no patient information, Jev placed up to 96% on a single diagnosis, while the comparators spread probability almost evenly. On the ophthalmic complaints, accuracy did not differ (Jev 88.8%, Opus 5 91.2%, Opus 5.5 88.8%), and Jev was better calibrated than the registered comparator (ECE difference -0.081, 95% CI -0.124 to -0.018). Conclusions: The decision model matched frontier models on short, distinctive ophthalmic complaints but fell well behind on multi-symptom synthetic patients, including behind a comparator without reasoning, and there it excluded the correct diagnosis outright in about 1 in 16 cases. Its probabilities signaled uncertainty only when the question offered a way to abstain. Calibration claims for clinical decision models should be tested on clinical tasks, with explicit abstention options and zero-probability rates reported.

items.title_en: Diagnostic accuracy and clinician-rated reasoning quality dissociate in a blinded evaluation of large language models in psychiatry
items.abstract_en: Background: Evaluations of large language models (LLMs) in medicine rest largely on diagnostic accuracy. We report what we learned evaluating four frontier LLMs on psychiatric diagnosis, where we asked whether clinician assessment of model reasoning adds information that accuracy does not. Methods: Four LLMs produced ranked five-diagnosis differentials for 196 psychiatric vignettes (135 screened published case reports; 61 unpublished, clinician-authored). An automated adjudicator scored accuracy. On a random 30-vignette subset, five psychiatrists blinded to model identity judged correctness and rated reasoning on a 0-4 rubric adapted from the ACGME Psychiatry Milestones. We validated the adjudicator against the clinicians, measured the reproducibility of accuracy across generation runs and repeated adjudication, and tested whether computable reasoning trace features could substitute for clinician ratings. Results: On all 196 vignettes, automated top-5 accuracy ranged from 0.759 to 0.837, and the majority verdict of three adjudication passes separated one of six model pairs. On the 30 rated vignettes, clinician-determined accuracy separated no pair, while reasoning separated five. Two systems were equally accurate (0.827 each; difference bounded within +/-0.059, or +/-0.10 after Holm adjustment) yet differed by 0.70 reasoning points (95% CI, 0.50 to 0.90). The adjudicator agreed with held-out clinician majorities less closely than individual clinicians did (0.83 to 0.85 vs 0.89 to 0.96), regeneration changed top-1 correctness for 18 of 119 pairs, and reference strings that combined several diagnoses were scored as misses until split. Trace features that tracked ratings across model averages did not track them across individual traces. Conclusions: Accuracy did not distinguish models that clinicians rated differently, and automated accuracy depended on how it was scored. Where LLMs are meant to support clinical reasoning, structured clinician assessment of reasoning belongs in pre-deployment evaluation.

items.title_en: A Methodology to Evaluate the Efficacy and Patient-Centeredness of a Patient-Facing AI Chatbot: Development and Validation of a Standardized-Patient Method
items.abstract_en: Background: Patient-facing AI intake chatbots can enter clinical use without regulatory review, so their errors may first surface with actual patients. Objective: To develop and pilot a remote, voice-based standardized patient (SP) method for evaluating an intake chatbot's history-taking, documentation, and patient-centeredness. Methods: Four primary care cases had Easy and Difficult variants. In Phase 1, five SPs completed 40 encounters with internal medicine residents rating portrayal fidelity. In Phase 2, SPs completed 80 encounters with a ChatGPT 4o chatbot, recorded whether critical elements were asked about and addressed satisfactorily, and rated summaries; four debriefing interviews were analyzed. In Phase 3, two blinded clinicians rated transcripts and summaries from 101 encounters (32 resident-led, 69 chatbot-led). Results: Portrayal fidelity averaged 4.52 of 5. The chatbot asked about 59.3% of critical elements in Easy versus 50.2% in Difficult variants (adjusted OR 1.49; 95% CI, 1.15 to 1.93) and addressed 73.3% versus 64.6% (OR 1.47; 1.12 to 1.93); near-ceiling summary quality did not differ. SPs reported missed information and rushed pacing. Reviewer agreement was moderate to substantial for element judgments (AC1 0.49 to 0.70) but poor for totals (ICC 0.10 and 0.21). In exploratory comparisons, residents asked about more elements (adjusted difference 12.5 percentage points; 95% CI, 7.0 to 18.1) and satisfactorily addressed more (9.2 points; 3.8 to 14.6); totals did not differ. Conclusions: SP portrayal was consistent enough for pre-clinical chatbot evaluation, and the method detected lower coverage in harder cases. Documentation ratings alone may miss conversational gaps, which require direct measurement.

items.title_en: Metabolic modulation of brain network dynamics during alcohol withdrawal
items.abstract_en: Chronic heavy alcohol use shifts brain metabolism from glucose toward acetate utilization. Sudden decreases in acetate following alcohol cessation in individuals with alcohol use disorder (AUD) may create an energetic imbalance that contributes to craving and withdrawal. A recent randomized study found that, compared with a standard American (SA) diet, a ketogenic diet (KD) during alcohol detoxification reduced withdrawal severity and craving and increased ketones and glutamate in the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex. These findings suggest that ketones may support metabolic adaptation during alcohol withdrawal, but the effects of altered brain metabolism on neural dynamics and alcohol cue reactivity remain unknown. Here, we used a control theoretic approach to test whether shifts in cerebral energy substrate utilization influence large-scale network dynamics through altered information flow. We analyzed fMRI cue-reactivity scans collected after one, two, and three weeks of inpatient treatment during presentation of alcohol, food, and neutral cues. Whole-brain effective connectivity was estimated using Shannon transfer entropy applied to whole brain atlas-aligned fMRI time series. Assuming neural activity flow along effective connections, we identified distinct shifts in the state-transition landscape in participants receiving the KD compared with the SA diet. Increases in serum {beta}-hydroxybutyrate (BHB) were associated with changes in state-transition landscape organization, which were in turn associated with reduced cue-induced alcohol craving. These findings link metabolic adaptation to large-scale neural dynamics and clinically relevant behavior and suggest that cerebral energy substrate availability may shape behavior by altering the organization of large-scale neural dynamics.

items.title_en: Persistent Hypertension After Asymptomatic Elevated In-Hospital Blood Pressure: The INDEBP Study
items.abstract_en: Background: Elevated blood pressure (BP) is common during hospitalization. Despite recommendations to avoid routine changes in antihypertensive therapy, clinical practice remains variable. Prospective data on whether elevated in-hospital BP identifies patients with hypertension after discharge are limited. Methods: Adults hospitalized for non-cardiac conditions with asymptomatic routine in-hospital BP ?140 and/or ?90 mmHg on at least two occasions separated by ?24 hours were prospectively enrolled. Antihypertensive therapy was managed at the discretion of treating physicians. Routine in-hospital BP, standardized research BP, and changes in antihypertensive therapy were recorded. Four weeks after discharge, participants underwent 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring (ABPM). Results: Among 50 participants, 42 (84%; 95% CI, 70.9 ? 92.8) had hypertension on follow-up ABPM. Among 21 participants without known hypertension, 18 (86%) had previously unrecognized hypertension on follow-up ABPM; among 29 participants with known hypertension, 24 (83%) had uncontrolled hypertension. Antihypertensive therapy was changed during hospitalization in 26 participants (52%), with de-escalation more frequent than intensification. Hypertension on follow-up ABPM was present in 88.5% of participants with and 79.2% without in-hospital therapy changes. Standardized research BP, but not routine in-hospital BP, correlated with follow-up ABPM. Conclusion: Asymptomatic elevated routine in-hospital BP identified a population with a high prevalence of hypertension four weeks after discharge, including patients with and without previously diagnosed hypertension. These findings support structured post-discharge BP reassessment rather than assuming that elevated in-hospital BP is transient. URL: www.ClinicalTrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT06132451

items.title_en: Association of Age With Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy and Left Ventricular Reverse Remodeling
items.abstract_en: Background: Comprehensive guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) remains underused in older patients with HFrEF, but whether the potential for treatment-associated myocardial recovery is preserved with advancing age remains uncertain. Objectives: To characterize age-related GDMT gaps and determine whether GDMT intensity is associated with left ventricular (LV) reverse remodeling across age and subsequent outcomes. Methods: We studied 1,795 patients with HFrEF receiving angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI)-based therapy in the multicenter STRATS-HF-ARNI registry. GDMT intensity was defined by the number of foundational therapies used during the first year after ARNI initiation. Serial LV remodeling and subsequent death or HF hospitalization were evaluated using multivariable models and a 1-year landmark analysis. Results: Triple/quadruple GDMT was achieved in 59.1%, 50.8%, 53.4%, and 43.0% of patients aged <60, 60-69, 70-79, and [≥]80 years, respectively (P<0.001). Older age and renal dysfunction independently predicted less comprehensive GDMT. Each additional GDMT pillar was associated with greater improvements in LVEF (+1.23 percentage-points; P=0.012) and LV global longitudinal strain (+0.32 percentage-points; P=0.049) and greater reductions in LV volumes. Substantial remodeling remained evident at advanced age. Greater LV reverse remodeling predicted lower subsequent risk, and exploratory bootstrap analyses supported significant indirect associations between greater GDMT intensity and lower risk through all four LV remodeling measures. Conclusions: Older patients received less comprehensive GDMT despite preserved potential for LV reverse remodeling. Greater GDMT intensity was associated with greater myocardial recovery, which may represent a pathway to better prognosis. These findings support intensive GDMT implementation in older patients when clinically tolerated.

items.title_en: A Novel Digital Phenotype of Physical Activity: Associations with Heart Rate Fragmentation
items.abstract_en: Background Heart rate fragmentation (HRF) has emerged as a novel marker of sinoatrial instability and neuroautonomic dysregulation and is a predictor of incident cardiovascular disease (CVD) events and cardiovascular mortality. Leveraging heart rate fragmentation as a novel measure may help us better understand the prognostic significance of physical activity. Physical activity (PA) patterns are multidimensional and difficult to study holistically, however. We sought to examine for novel PA clusters in a cohort of veteran men and evaluate their prognostic significance based on their associations with neuroautonomic dysregulation. Methods In this cross-sectional study, we examined 602 male veterans from the Vietnam Era Twins Study of Electrophysiology in Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (VETS-EP) who were enrolled between 2022 and 2026. Accelerometry data were used to derive physical activity parameters across 6 domains: volume, sedentary behavior, intensity, diurnal pattern, fragmentation, and variability. Heart rate fragmentation was assessed using percentage of inflection points (PIP), inverse average length of segments (IALS), percentage of short segments (PSS), and percentage of alternating segments (PAS). Gaussian mixture models were used to derive digital phenotypes of physical activity, and associations with heart rate fragmentation were assessed using linear mixed models. Results Participants had a mean age of 73.8 {+/-} 2.9 years and 93.2% reported White race. Two overlapping phenotypes of physical activity patterns were identified: a compact-early phenotype, characterized by earlier activity timing and slightly greater overall activity, and a diffuse-late phenotype, characterized by later activity timing and greater heterogeneity in activity volume. In fully adjusted models, the diffuse-late phenotype was associated with higher PIP, the primary outcome ({beta}: 1.199, 95% CI: 0.034 to 2.363, p-value: 0.044), and higher IALS ({beta}: 0.01210, 95% CI: 0.00048 to 0.02373, p-value: 0.041), but not PSS or PAS, compared with the compact-early phenotype. Conclusions In older male veterans, Gaussian mixture model phenotyping identified two overlapping physical activity phenotypes, differing mainly in diurnal timing and in the dispersion of overall activity, that were associated with modest differences in heart rate fragmentation. These phenotypes provide a framework for capturing complex physical activity patterns. Future prospective studies representing diverse populations are needed to validate such phenotypes.

items.title_en: Laboratory Evaluation of Cyclospora cayetanensis in Wastewater: Expanding Pathogen Targets for Regulatory Public Health Surveillance
items.abstract_en: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has become a cornerstone of public health surveillance, yet routine regulatory monitoring remains largely focused on respiratory viruses and selecting antimicrobial resistant bacteria. Emerging foodborne parasites, such as Cyclospora cayetanensis, remain excluded from standard environmental surveillance panels despite increasing domestic outbreaks. This study presents a laboratory-based pilot protocol evaluating the feasibility of extracting and quantifying C. cayetanensis from urban wastewater across the Chicago metropolitan area. Using sample concentration via centrifugation and mechanical bead-beating, automated magnetic bead nucleic acid extraction, and digital PCR (dPCR), we demonstrate high-sensitivity detection in municipal influents and sewer nodes. These findings establish a proof-of-concept laboratory methodology to support the expansion of regulatory public health surveillance frameworks to include non-routine protozoan pathogens.

items.title_en: From examinations to consultations: a physician-reviewed Japanese benchmark for large language models in traditional Kampo medicine
items.abstract_en: Objectives: Patients and clinicians increasingly ask large language models (LLMs) about Kampo, Japan's traditional medicine. Yet evaluations of LLMs have measured accuracy on examination questions, which ask what a model knows; a consultation asks whether it can apply that knowledge to the patient at hand. No benchmark had measured that. Materials and Methods: KampoBench comprises 74 consultation scenarios and 310 conversation-specific rubric criteria, following the design of HealthBench. Scenarios, criteria and reference answers were drafted by an LLM and revised by board-certified Kampo physicians. Ten current models from three vendors were evaluated. Because LLM graders are known to favor their own family, each response was graded by a model from each vendor. Results: The best model reached 74.8-86.3% across graders, the physician-revised reference answers 87.9-92.4%. Rankings were stable across graders (Spearman's rho 0.952-0.976), and the family-favoring deviation was 0.4 to 0.6 percentage points, below the bootstrap standard deviation of one measurement; grader leniency varied by 14.3 points. Models were most reliable on criteria about advising that care be sought (83.6%) and least reliable on those requiring a known crude-drug risk to be tied to the case (17.5%), though 79.2% of those responses named the drug. Discussion: The shortfall lay in applying knowledge to the case rather than in holding it - a distinction examination-format evaluations cannot make. Conclusion: Evaluation in traditional medicine should measure the judgments a consultation requires, not recall alone. Quoted alongside the grader that produced it, a KampoBench score is a usable measure of those judgments.

items.title_en: Pressure is not flow: Rethinking blood pressure as a surrogate for cerebral blood flow during general anesthesia
items.abstract_en: Abstract Background: Mean arterial pressure (MAP) is pharmacologically augmented in selected perioperative and critical care settings, including acute neurological conditions and after cardiac arrest, with the aim of improving cerebral perfusion, although it remains uncertain whether higher arterial pressure translates into increased cerebral blood flow (CBF). We investigated the CBF response to MAP augmentation with norepinephrine (NE), a commonly used vasopressor in perioperative and critical care settings, during propofol-based general anesthesia. Methods: In this prospective within-subject interventional study, 16 neurologically intact patients with ASA physical status I-II undergoing elective surgery were studied using phase-contrast magnetic resonance imaging. CBF was quantified in the awake state and during propofol-based general anesthesia before and after NE-induced MAP augmentation. During general anesthesia, NE was titrated to increase MAP by approximately 25% from baseline. Concurrent systemic hemodynamics were assessed. Results: General anesthesia was associated with a 50.1% (interquartile range, 42.1?55.7%) reduction in CBF and a 24.2% (20.3-29.2%) reduction in MAP compared with the awake state (both P<0.001). During general anesthesia, NE-induced MAP augmentation increased MAP by 25.7% (21.9-32.0%; P<0.001), whereas CBF remained unchanged (P=1.000). Cardiac output remained unchanged (P=0.163), whereas systemic vascular resistance index and cerebrovascular resistance increased by 40.0% (28.7-45.2%) and 36.2% (17.7-42.8%), respectively (both P<0.001). Changes in CBF during MAP augmentation were not associated with concurrent changes in MAP, cardiac output, or systemic vascular resistance index. Conclusions: In neurologically intact patients undergoing propofol-based general anesthesia, clinically relevant NE-induced MAP augmentation did not increase CBF despite an approximately 50% lower CBF than in the awake state. These findings challenge the assumption that pharmacological elevation of an otherwise adequate MAP improves cerebral perfusion in this setting. While maintaining adequate arterial pressure remains essential, further MAP augmentation should not be assumed to increase CBF. Clinical Trial Registration: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06855407; NCT06855407.

items.title_en: Pulsed Field Versus Radiofrequency Ablation For Repeat Ablation of Atrial Fibrillation: Evaluation of Outcomes
items.abstract_en: Background Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) has recently been approved in the USA as a new method for treating atrial fibrillation (AF). PFA provides a promising new approach in the treatment of atrial fibrillation (AF), which historically has a high recurrence rate post-ablation. Of significance, PFA has shown promising data in terms of safety and procedural efficiency to radiofrequency ablation (RFA). Objective The purpose of this study was to compare the procedural and health outcomes in patients with recurrent AF undergoing ablation using PFA or RFA. Methods Consecutive patients with a history of previous radiofrequency ablation and recurrent AF undergoing redo ablation with PFA or RFA were included. Patients were seen for follow-up in the clinic ranging from 4 months to a year and we reported ablation strategy and arrhythmia type. The primary outcome was recurrence of any atrial arrhythmia after a 90-day blanking period.
